case_name: Hey Listen Mandyhan, L.L.C. v. Trody

issues.label: Court subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must have statutory authority to hear an FED action versus requiring a different civil action (e.g., foreclosure).

issues.label: Proper venue in Lucas County
issues.why: The action must be brought in the correct municipal/county court where the property is located.

issues.label: Standing/real party in interest
issues.why: Plaintiff must prove it is the owner/entitled to possession and is the proper party to sue.

issues.label: Authority of Mandyhan agent
issues.why: The court must determine whether Mark Grabow/others had authority to bind Mandyhan to the lease/purchase terms.

issues.label: Existence of landlord-tenant relationship
issues.why: An FED claim generally requires proof of a tenancy and wrongful holding over after termination.

issues.label: Existence of vendor-vendee relationship
issues.why: If the arrangement is a land installment contract, the proper remedy and notices differ from eviction.

issues.label: Characterization of agreements
issues.why: The court must decide whether the contemporaneous lease and purchase agreement together form a single transaction and what it legally is.

issues.label: Integration clause effect
issues.why: The lease’s integration clause may bar use of the purchase agreement to alter lease terms unless an exception applies.

issues.label: Parol evidence admissibility
issues.why: If the writings are integrated/unambiguous, extrinsic evidence of intent may be limited; if ambiguous, it may be allowed.

issues.label: Ambiguity determination
issues.why: The court must decide whether the documents are ambiguous and, if so, construe them under contract-interpretation rules.

issues.label: Option to purchase vs sale
issues.why: The court must determine whether the purchase agreement is an option contingent on lease compliance or a present sale contract.

issues.label: Land installment contract definition
issues.why: The court must apply R.C. 5313.01 et seq. to decide if the arrangement qualifies as a land installment contract.

issues.label: Residential property requirement
issues.why: R.C. 5313.01(B) requires real property improved by a dwelling; the court must decide if a dwelling exists on the parcel.

issues.label: Meaning of 'dwelling' here
issues.why: The court must interpret whether conversion of part of a garage into living space can constitute a dwelling under R.C. 5313.01(B).

issues.label: Whether dwelling must be erected
issues.why: The court must decide if the statute requires a dwelling to have been erected as a residence (or newly erected) versus adapted from an existing structure.

issues.label: Effect of commercial zoning
issues.why: The court must decide whether zoning classification or illegality of residential occupancy affects 'dwelling' status or enforceability/remedy.

issues.label: Illegality/public policy defense
issues.why: If residential use violates zoning/building codes, the court must consider whether that makes the contract/occupancy unenforceable or affects remedies.

issues.label: Building-code habitability issues
issues.why: If the structure is not a lawful dwelling, that may affect whether 5313 applies and whether tenant protections apply.

issues.label: R.C. 5313.02 compliance
issues.why: If a land installment contract exists, the court must check whether statutory formal requirements were met.

issues.label: Substantial compliance doctrine
issues.why: If strict 5313.02 compliance is lacking, the court must decide whether substantial compliance can validate/enforce the agreement and with what consequences.

issues.label: Consequences of noncompliance
issues.why: If 5313.02 requirements are not met, the court must determine what remedies/penalties apply and whether eviction is permitted.

issues.label: Down payment characterization
issues.why: The court must decide whether the $3,000 was a security deposit, a down payment, or both, affecting default and forfeiture analysis.

issues.label: Monthly payment characterization
issues.why: The court must determine whether the $459.10/$570/$574 payments are rent, installment payments, or a hybrid allocation.

issues.label: Taxes/insurance allocation
issues.why: The court must decide whether extra monthly amounts for taxes/insurance show installment-contract characteristics or merely additional rent/charges.

issues.label: Assessments/taxes clause significance
issues.why: Requiring the occupant to pay taxes/assessments may indicate a land sale arrangement; the court must weigh this in intent/classification.

issues.label: Default date and amount
issues.why: The court must determine when default occurred (March 1 vs April/May) and the amount of arrears to evaluate termination/cure rights.

issues.label: Tender and refusal effect
issues.why: Trody’s attempted payment after notice and Mandyhan’s refusal may affect whether default was cured, waived, or still actionable.

issues.label: Waiver/acceptance course of dealing
issues.why: The history of accepting payments and any late payments may create waiver or require notice before strict enforcement.

issues.label: Notice requirements under R.C. 1923
issues.why: For an FED action, the landlord must serve a valid three-day notice meeting statutory content and service requirements.

issues.label: Notice requirements under R.C. 5313.06
issues.why: If the arrangement is a land installment contract, a ten-day notice to cure delinquency is required before forfeiture/eviction-type action.

issues.label: Which notice regime controls
issues.why: The court must decide whether 1923’s three-day notice or 5313’s ten-day cure notice applies based on contract classification.

issues.label: Validity of posted notice service
issues.why: The court must determine whether posting by Hill satisfied statutory service methods and whether the notice content was compliant.

issues.label: Termination of tenancy
issues.why: If a lease governs, the court must decide whether the lease was properly terminated for nonpayment before filing FED.

issues.label: Forfeiture vs foreclosure remedy
issues.why: If it is a land installment contract, the court must decide whether forfeiture is available or foreclosure is required.

issues.label: 20 percent payment threshold
issues.why: Under R.C. 5313.07, if the vendee paid 20% or more, seller must foreclose; the court must compute the percentage correctly.

issues.label: How to compute 20 percent paid
issues.why: The court must decide what counts as payments toward purchase price (excluding interest, taxes, insurance, or rent) when applying R.C. 5313.07.

issues.label: Evidentiary sufficiency of ledger
issues.why: The court must decide whether the payment ledger is admissible/credible and whether it proves payments and allocation to principal/interest.

issues.label: Judicial notice propriety
issues.why: The court must rule whether it can take judicial notice of calculations/ledger totals versus requiring proof through evidence.

issues.label: Magistrate procedure compliance
issues.why: The court must ensure the magistrate hearing and decision complied with Civ.R. 53 requirements.

issues.label: Objections standard of review
issues.why: The trial court must independently review objected matters and apply proper deference/credibility standards to the magistrate’s findings.

issues.label: Credibility determinations
issues.why: Resolution of intent and contract characterization depends on witness credibility, which the factfinder must address.

issues.label: Use of zoning testimony opinion
issues.why: The court must consider whether Marie’s belief about zoning permissibility was admissible lay opinion and what weight it should receive.

issues.label: Relevance of improvements and assent
issues.why: Trody’s renovations with alleged approval may evidence intent to sell or estoppel; the court must consider their legal significance.

issues.label: Equitable estoppel/part performance
issues.why: Conduct like allowing residential conversion and accepting payments may estop Mandyhan from denying sale/5313 protections or may support enforcement.

issues.label: Unclean hands/illegal occupancy equities
issues.why: If both parties knowingly allowed illegal residential use, the court may need to consider equitable consequences in choosing remedies.

issues.label: Scope of FED adjudication
issues.why: The court must decide what issues are permissible in an FED (possession) versus requiring separate action for title/contract claims.

issues.label: Title dispute limitation
issues.why: If deciding land installment contract status effectively adjudicates title interests, the court must ensure it stays within FED limits or dismisses.

issues.label: Remedy if contract is LIC
issues.why: If a land installment contract exists, the court must decide whether to dismiss FED, require foreclosure, or convert proceedings as allowed.

issues.label: Attorney fees/costs entitlement
issues.why: The court must determine any statutory/contractual entitlement to costs or fees in FED or related default.

issues.label: Proper judgment form and writ
issues.why: If possession is awarded, the court must ensure the judgment and any writ of restitution comply with statutory requirements.
